title: Finite splitting filtration by separated etale scheme neighborhoods
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and atlas point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A space is quasi-compact if every open cover of its point space has a finite subcover, and quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback to every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source, and quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. An affine morphism is representable by schemes and has affine source after every affine scheme test. Local finite presentation and local finite type are tested on compatible etale scheme charts [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]; finite presentation means local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness.  An open subspace is represented on each scheme test by an open subscheme [def-a1-space-open-subspace]; a closed immersion is represented on each scheme test by a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Etale morphisms are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and let $X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. There are an integer $n\geq1$, quasi-compact open subspaces $\emptyset=U_{n+1}\subset U_n\subset\cdots\subset U_1=X$, quasi-compact separated schemes $V_p$ for $1\leq p\leq n$, and representable surjective etale maps $f_p:V_p\to U_p$ such that, for $T_p=U_p\setminus U_{p+1}$ with its reduced closed subspace structure, $V_p\times_{U_p}T_p\to T_p$ is an isomorphism. Reduced closed structure means the closed subspace defined on etale affine charts by the radical ideal of the closed subset. In addition $f_n:V_n\to U_n$ is an isomorphism, so $U_n$ is a quasi-compact separated scheme. Separated for a scheme means that its absolute diagonal is a closed immersion. The empty space is allowed.

source.place: Tag 07ST (lemma-filter-quasi-compact-quasi-separated); last stratum is schematic as explained in spaces-limits.tex, proposition-approximate, first proof paragraph

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale chart $a:U\to X$ with $U$ affine by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-qc-etale-fibre-bound] to this quasi-compact scheme and the quasi-separated space $X$, obtaining a uniform geometric fibre bound $d\geq0$. Put $n=\max(1,d)$. This also handles $X=\varnothing$, for then $U=\varnothing$ and all the constructions below are empty.

source.place: Tag 07ST (lemma-filter-quasi-compact-quasi-separated), boundedness reduction to Tag 03JX; Tag 0BBN (lemma-filter-quasi-compact), initial affine atlas.

proof.text: For $1\leq p\leq n+1$ use [lem-sfb-etale-atlas-distinct-tuple-geometry] to form the quasi-compact separated scheme $W_p$ of ordered pairwise distinct $p$-tuples in $U$ over $X$. Its comparison to the affine absolute product $U^p$ is separated and locally quasi-finite. Its restriction to the open $W_p$ stays separated and locally quasi-finite by [lem-a1-space-separated-lqf-permanence]. Thus [lem-sfb-separated-lqf-affine-finite-set] supplies an affine open containing any prescribed finite set in $W_p$. The symmetric group $S_p$ acts by permuting coordinates. This action is free on every scheme test: equality of two permuted tuples with different permutations forces equality of two distinct coordinates on any nonempty component, forbidden by the definition of $W_p$. Each point orbit is finite and hence lies in an affine open. Apply [lem-sfb-admissible-free-finite-quotient] to obtain $q_p:W_p\to V_p=W_p/S_p$, finite etale surjective, with $V_p$ a quasi-compact separated scheme.

source.place: Tag 0BBN (lemma-filter-quasi-compact), first paragraph, using Tag 07S0, Tag 07S6 and Tag 0BBM; quasi-compactness from Tag 07ST.

proof.text: The map $W_p\to X$ is invariant under $S_p$, so the quotient universal property in [lem-sfb-admissible-free-finite-quotient] gives $b_p:V_p\to X$. The composite with $q_p$ is representable etale by Step 2. Since $q_p$ is a surjective etale scheme morphism, clause (1) of [lem-trf-space-etale-source-atlas-detection] says $b_p$ is representable etale. By [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image], its image is an open subspace $U_p$, it factors as a representable surjective etale map $f_p:V_p\to U_p$, and $U_p$ is quasi-compact since $V_p$ is.

source.place: Tag 0BBN (lemma-filter-quasi-compact), end of first paragraph and beginning of second; source-local etaleness Tag 03FS.

proof.text: For any algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$, Step 2 identifies the fibre of $W_p(\Omega)$ with ordered distinct $p$-tuples in the finite set $E=U(\Omega)\times_{X(\Omega)}\{\bar x\}$. The geometric orbit clause of [lem-sfb-admissible-free-finite-quotient] identifies the fibre of $V_p(\Omega)$ with its $S_p$-orbits, hence with the $p$-element subsets of $E$. Thus $\bar x$ belongs to $U_p$ exactly when $|E|\geq p$. Membership in the image is tested after a field extension by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]; a nonempty geometric fibre already has an $\Omega$-point: [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests] makes it an etale scheme over $\Omega$; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] writes it as a disjoint union of finite separable spectra, and [lem-weil-pbc-alg-closed-finite-extension-trivial] identifies each residue extension with $\Omega$. Therefore the same criterion holds on underlying point classes. Surjectivity of $a$ gives $U_1=X$, and $|E|\leq d\leq n$ gives $U_{n+1}=\varnothing$. The criterion gives $|U_{p+1}|\subseteq|U_p|$; the open-subspace order assertion of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] gives the required inclusions of subspaces.

source.place: Tag 0BBN (lemma-filter-quasi-compact), second paragraph; termination as in Tag 07S9, with Tag 03JX bound from Step 1.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] put on $|U_p|\setminus|U_{p+1}|$ its reduced closed subspace structure $T_p\hookrightarrow U_p$. The pullback $Z_p=V_p\times_{U_p}T_p\to T_p$ is representable surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. It is separated: on every scheme test its relative diagonal is the pullback of the absolute closed diagonal of $V_p$ along the natural map from the relative double product to the absolute double product; on scheme tests the required closedness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] and [def-weil-closed-immersion]. At a geometric point of $T_p$, Step 4 gives $|E|=p$, so its fibre has exactly one point (the unique $p$-element subset of $E$). By [lem-sfb-space-separated-etale-diagonal-complement], a separated surjective etale morphism with these singleton geometric fibres is an isomorphism. This proves the splitting on each stratum.

source.place: Tag 0BBN (lemma-filter-quasi-compact), second paragraph, the maps Z_p to T_p, and Tag 05W5.

proof.text: Finally $U_{n+1}=\varnothing$, so $T_n$ has all the point classes of $U_n$. Every geometric point of $U_n$ consequently has the singleton fibre computed in Step 5: the inclusion of the reduced closed subspace does not change field-valued points, since every map from a field kills every nilpotent in each chart. The map $f_n:V_n\to U_n$ is separated by the same absolute-diagonal pullback calculation as Step 5 and is surjective etale by Step 3. Apply [lem-sfb-space-separated-etale-diagonal-complement] once more to conclude that $f_n$ is an isomorphism. Thus $U_n$ is the quasi-compact separated scheme $V_n$. All assertions, including $n\geq1$ and the empty case, now hold.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q24-01db86eb5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS with no changes. I read Stacks 0BBN, 07ST, 07S6/07S7 and 0BBM(4) in full, and the item's statement agrees with 07ST. The qc of U_p and the claim that f_n is an isomorphism are the 07SU additions, and both are true. Steps: (1) the affine atlas and the fibre bound d need only |X| qc and X quasi-separated, and n=max(1,d). (2) W_p→U^p is separated and lqf, so S_p-orbits lie in affines. Freeness holds on T-points, because the components where g≠g' fall into Δ_ij, which misses W_p. The quotient node gives V_p. (3) The universal property gives b_p, clause (1) of source-atlas-detection gives étaleness, and the open-image lemma gives U_p, f_p and qc. (4) The Ω-fibre of V_p is the set of p-subsets of E. Ω-points versus points goes through scheme-tests, the étale-fibre lemma and the alg-closed leaf, so x∈U_p iff |E|≥p. This gives U_1=X, U_{n+1}=∅ and nestedness. (5) The relative diagonal is the pullback of the absolute diagonal, which I checked, so Z_p→T_p is separated étale surjective with singleton fibres and the diagonal-complement criterion makes it an isomorphism. (6) Since U_{n+1}=∅, every point of U_n has |E|=n, so f_n is an isomorphism. Distinct-tuple geometry node: true, via 03KN (Δ_X is an unramified monomorphism) and the qc of Δ_X; cases p=1, U=∅ and X=∅ checked. Quotient node: true, since j is a finite monomorphism hence a closed immersion (0BBM); torsor Ω-points checked for trivial G, empty M and p | |G|. Neither node duplicates an existing node: lem-per-free-finite-group-affine-quotient needs an affine morphism, lem-sfb-finite-locally-free-open-affine-cover needs a source open in an affine, and lem-sfb-qc-space-schematic-strata gives only the strata. Neither restates the item. There is no cycle (my own closure check), no SGA citation, no supersession (live and side-live are unsplit) and no repair note. Batch 5: every flagged citation (def-trf-algebraic-space, trf fibre products, étale detection, scheme tests, and the a1/sfb space lemmas that reach trf only through the definition) is generic space foundation. None is a trace-formula or Poincaré step, so all are accepted. I accept the 12 tool_uses as local geometry from Stacks.

lean.statement: theorem exists_qcqs_splitting_filtration (X : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (hqc : CompactSpace (Point X.obj.obj)) (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated X) : ∃ (m : ℕ) (U : Fin (m + 2) → OpenSubspace X) (V : Fin (m + 1) → Over (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (f : ∀ p : Fin (m + 1), yoneda.obj (V p) ⟶ (U p.castSucc).val.toFunctor) (T : Fin (m + 1) → AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (t : ∀ p : Fin (m + 1), (T p).obj.obj ⟶ (U p.castSucc).val.toFunctor), (U 0).val = ⊤ ∧ (U (Fin.last (m + 1))).val = ⊥ ∧ (∀ p : Fin (m + 1), U p.succ ≤ U p.castSucc) ∧ (∀ p : Fin (m + 2), CompactSpace (Point (U p).val.toFunctor)) ∧ (∀ p : Fin (m + 1), CompactSpace (V p).left ∧ (V p).left.IsSeparated ∧ IsEtale (f p) ∧ IsSurjective (f p)) ∧ (∀ p : Fin (m + 1), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ q ↦ IsClosedImmersion q.left) (t p) ∧ IsReduced (T p) ∧ pointImage (t p) = mapPoint (U p.castSucc).val.ι ⁻¹' (pointImage (U p.succ).val.ι)ᶜ ∧ IsIso (Limits.pullback.snd (f p) (t p))) ∧ IsIso (f (Fin.last m))
